Posted March 23, 2006
Analysis by Richard Cowan
See
 Canadians Need to Examine The Role of the Police In Maintaining Marijuana Prohibition. Paying For Lies That Distort Public Policies and Undermine Sovereignty. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
 Lies Have Consequences: Police Targeted Anti-Prohibitionist Reporter Because They Believed Lies Told By Their Superiors  Who Are Shocked, Of Course.
and
 As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That
and
 Walters Concedes That Canada Can Legalize Cannabis If It Wants To, Which Was The Only True Thing He Said While In Montreal.

For many years now, I have been warning my Canadian friends about the role the RCMP is playing in undermining both the freedom of the Canadian people and the very sovereignty of Canada.
From 1999 see
 Canadian Police Lie to The Canadian Media Who Lie To Their Readers
To Justify More Power Over the Canadian People To Please DEAland Narks
An Utterly Wretched Piece Of Pseudo-journalism

It is true that Canadian law enforcement is less directly involved in politics than their American counterparts, because, unlike in the US, almost none are elected. There are no elected sheriffs and prosecutors, so they do not have the political organizations like those that control much of the US political system, especially the Republican Party.
See
 Its The Stupidity, Stupid. How the Prohibitionist Ideology Has Wrecked The Republican Party and Undermined Democracy Everywhere. When Ideology Trumps Reality, The Result is Stupidity.

Nonetheless, the RCMP escalated its involvement in politics during the January elections that brought a prohibitionist Conservative Party to power in a minority government. Less than 40% of Canadians voted for the Tories, and surveys consistently show that a majority of Canadian favor some sort of decrim, so it is clear that there is no mandate for escalating the war on marijuana users.

Consequently, the RCMP prohibitionist propaganda machine concentrates on the supposed threat from growers. Grow houses are portrayed as major fire hazards, even though the number of house fires in BC actually decreased from 6,030 to 4,693 between 1999 and 2003, when the number of grow ops was almost certainly increasing.
See
 RCMP Report On The Drug Situation in Canada  2004 Contradicts The Prohibitionist Party Line  Again. Mexico Supplies US With At Least 25 Times More Than Canada. Ontario Rivals British Columbia .  

Growers are almost always portrayed as being involved in organized crime  especially biker gangs and Vietnamese gangs. I have not yet heard any reports on Vietnamese bikers. They must be just too frightening to contemplate!! Usually, these reports include the cliché, People have a concept that these are ma and pa operations. They're anything but.

Actually, the above quote did not come directly from an RCMP officer, but from Daryl Plecas a BC criminologist who has done studies costing $250,000 on behalf of the RCMP.
From 2002 see
 The Agenda for the Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada. Analysis by Richard Cowan  

Last March, Shannon Kari, who is now with the Globe and Mail, wrote an excellent article for the CanWest news service (both Vancouver papers and the National Post, and others), Grow-op Study Blasted.
Excerpt:
Insp.  Paul Nadeau says the funds were a good use of RCMP resources and insisted the police force gave Darryl Plecas total freedom to conduct his research.  

"We just wanted the facts," says Nadeau, who heads the RCMP's co-ordinated marijuana enforcement unit in B.C.

"Who else was going to fund this type of project?" asked Plecas, who flatly rejected any suggestion the study was not independent.  "Just because police put in the money, it doesn't mean they want a whitewash."

Plecas, an experienced criminologist at the University College of the Fraser Valley, updated one of his previous studies -- also commissioned by the RCMP -- and examined police and prosecution statistics about marijuana cultivation in B.C.  from 1997 to 2003. See the above 2002 link  

The two studies cost a total of $250,000.  

The widely reported update, released this month, described marijuana grow-ops as a growing "risk to public safety," and called for more criminal justice resources to deal with the issue, as well as stiffer jail sentences.
See
 Would BC Have Less Bud if It Had More Prisoners? Lying to Canadians To Support the Cannabis Prohibition.     

Kari also reported that firearms were seized in six per cent of cases in B.C.  between 1997 and 2003, and Hard drugs like heroin or cocaine were found in less than four per cent of raids and fires in indoor grow-ops occurred in less than four per cent of cases.

It is very clear why Nadeau, the head of the RCMP's co-ordinated marijuana enforcement unit in B.C. thinks the study was a good deal  and it was, for the RCMP.

Nadeau was a major source for the New York Times contribution to the prohibitionist propaganda effort last year.
See
 Front Page Fantasy: The New York Times Pushes Fact Free Journalism Supposedly About BC Bud  

Nadeau was also a major source for a recent BBC report on BC Bud. Canada's growing marijuana problem

It was much more balanced than the New York Times piece, but not because of Nadeau.
Excerpts from the BBC:

"Cannabis is the biggest issue facing law enforcement now," says Inspector Paul Nadeau of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP)(emphasis added)

He calls for greater deterrents, pointing out that in BC only about 10%  of those convicted of growing marijuana face jail terms (the figure is higher in other provinces), with most offenders getting a fine or suspended sentence.

He says judges facing a backlog of cases in the courts "have to be given the means to deal with the problem... We are drowning in the numbers."

These are not just Nadeaus opinions. The BBC report also said, But police insist tougher sentences, not legalisation of cannabis, is what is needed

This argument is echoed by the new Ottawa government, though it says it will take advice before formulating a detailed drugs policy. It argues any resultant increase in spending on tougher law enforcement will be offset by lower spending on the social problems caused by drug abuse.

"Parents and police officers agree the last thing we need is more drugs on the streets," says the Ministry of Justice's acting communications director Patrick Charette. (emphasis added)

Notice that formulation: "Parents and police officers agree.. Or as Chairman Mao would put it, The great broad masses of the people

Last September, the prohibitionist Vancouver Province reported that Nadeau said the courts should hand out longer jail sentences to parents who raise their kids in marijuana drug houses. (MOUNTIE WANTS PARENTS PUNISHED FOR RAISING CHILDREN IN A GROW-OP)

Nadeau said it should become an aggravating factor in sentencing, just like having firearms or booby-traps on the premises.

The article also quotes Darryl Plecas, again. He now heads B.C.'s new Centre for Criminal Justice Research, and he agrees that stiffer jail sentences would act as a deterrent to criminals.

"I'm amazed that the courts haven't taken an extremely strong stance," he said.  "I would really question the ability of somebody to be considered an appropriate parent if they're placing their kids in that kind of situation.

 "I don't see any harm whatever in taking their kids away."

He doesnt see any harm in taking children away from their parents when plants are being grown in their house! Prohibitionist family values. I have several friends who are medical cannabis users and they have been threatened with the loss of their children. Some have had the police point guns at their children. A grow-op is not inherently dangerous. Raiding a house with guns drawn is inherently dangerous.

Of course, there is nothing new about governments buying research that supports its position, especially in DEAland.
See
 Voice of America Becomes Latest Organization to Be Corrupted By Cannabis Prohibition. Canadian Collaborators Lie To Undermine Their Countrys Freedom and Sovereignty. The Myth of BC Bud.
and
 How NIDA Made Monkeys of the Media. 4 Primates Are News; 4 Million People Are Not. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and links

However, it is puzzling that prohibitionist propaganda seems more successful in Canada. Even though far more of the major Canadian newspapers editorialize in favor of legalization  not just decrim  than in the US, there seems to be more support for legalization in the US than in the supposedly more liberal Canada. 

Last week, NORML reported that a scientific poll taken by Zogby showed that almost half of the citizens of DEAland are in favor of legalization, which does not seem to be the case in Canada.
From NORML See
 Zogby Poll: Nearly Half Of Americans Believe Pot Should Be Regulated Like Alcohol -- Majorities In The East And West Coasts Back Legalization 

One reason may be that Canadians really like the RCMP, even though their trust is badly misplaced. Americans, on the other hand, are more skeptical about the police and are becoming increasingly alienated from their government and really do not trust the mass media (AKA the drug czars steno pool.)
See
 Bush Should Have John  Comical Ali  Walters Explain The Iraq War, Then The Media Would Never Ask Any Embarrassing Questions. Doctrine Of Drug Czar Infallibility? Blame Canada, Again.  

While this skepticism is encouraging for those of us who think that the Bush Administration is both incompetent and dishonest, it is also indicative of very serious problems in the American democracy.
See
 We Live In Interesting Times. The Elections and the Cannabis Reform Movement. The Problems With Making Democracy Work Against Prohibitionist Propaganda.  

Of course, the medical cannabis issue is the most extreme example of the disconnect between the politicians and the people. The public overwhelmingly opposes arresting sick people who are using cannabis medically. Nonetheless, even the state politicians, who are supposed to be closest to the people, still defer to the police on the issue, although that is beginning to change. There is no other issue with comparable public support that is so frightening to the politicians. What are they afraid of?
See
 Leakin Bout My G-G-Generation. Leak of AARP Poll On Medical Cannabis Assures Story Will Have Long Legs. Mainstreaming Real Threat To Prohibitionist Party Line.  

As odd as it may seem, the anti-prohibitionist movement in America is actually much more effective than it is in Canada  or almost anywhere else in the world. One can see the current split in American public opinion over the Iraq war as typical of the controversy about the drugwar. If the American media stop playing steno pool for the czar, the DEAland police establishment will not be able to sustain its hold on the politicians. Freedom will prevail.
See
 Lou Dobbs and the Second Mexican War. Has It Already Begun? Counting the Costs of the Drugwar.
